question: In an industrial chemical equilibrium investigation at constant temperature in a 7.1 dm³ reactor: A(g) + 2B(g) ⇌ C(g). If equilibrium yield produces 3.050 mol of product C, what would be the effect on the equilibrium concentration of C if the reactor volume is halved to 3.55 dm³?
correct_answer: The concentration of C will more than double (it increases both due to the volume halving and due to the equilibrium shifting to the right toward fewer gaseous moles).
wrong_answers_pool: The concentration of C will remain exactly the same.

The value of Kc will double.
explanation: Halving volume instantly doubles all concentrations; then, because 3 moles of gas -> 1 mole of gas, the equilibrium shifts to the right, increasing [C] even further.

tags.learning_outcome: Evaluate volume change on non-equimolar gas equilibrium

question: In a 10 kg bag of fertilizer marked **3 : 1 : 5 (26)**, what is the total mass of inert filler material (such as gypsum, sand, or limestone)?
explanation: The active fertilizer content is 26%, so inert filler makes up 100% - 26% = 74%. Mass of filler = 10 × (74/100) = 7.40 kg.
